title: Tanzanian Green Banana and Beans
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Ndizi na Maharage — green cooking bananas and beans simmered together in a spiced tomato sauce. The complete plant-based protein meal of Tanzania's highland regions — the banana provides starch, the beans provide protein, together they provide everything.
longDesc: Green banana and beans is one of Tanzania's most nutritionally complete plant-based meals — the combination of starchy banana and protein-rich beans forms a naturally complete food. In the Kilimanjaro highlands where this dish originates, it has sustained communities for centuries.
ingredients: 4 large green cooking bananas — peeled and halved
200g kidney beans — soaked and cooked until tender
steps: Peel bananas wearing gloves. Halve and submerge in salted water.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices, tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes.
Add bananas and water. Simmer covered 20—25 minutes until nearly tender.
Add cooked beans. Simmer 10 more minutes.
The sauce should be thick and coating.
chefTips: Wear gloves when peeling bananas — the latex sap stains permanently.
Bananas take longer than beans — add them first.
The starch from the bananas thickens the sauce naturally.
cookingScience: Green banana resistant starch dissolves partially into the cooking liquid during simmering — naturally thickening the sauce while also providing prebiotic fibre that feeds beneficial gut bacteria.
sustainabilityTips: Both green bananas and beans are produced locally in Tanzania's highland regions.
healthBenefits: Rich in potassium, iron, and fibre.
culturalNote: Green banana and beans is the Kilimanjaro highlands' most complete food — the combination that sustained the Chagga communities who farmed the fertile slopes of Africa's highest mountain for centuries.
